item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded: EagleKnight9, instead of replying to your own comments and posting multiple comments in succession, please edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of every comment. That prevents spam buildup, and it's in the rules.

item.title: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
I have another narrative idea where Sir Reginald could unknowingly manifest different characters from the fictional universe he originated from as a kind of coping mechanism, as he tries to come to terms with his "unrealness".

This effect could be explained as the SCP making Sir Reginald a reality bender, the SCP itself just being Sir Reginald as an anomalous reality bender, the SCP generating the characters as an effect of Sir Reginald's belief that the characters are real, or Sir Reginald being a reality bender in his reality, with his powers transferring through realities.

I would like feedback for if this would be a good way to construct/add on to the narrative stated above.

item.title: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded: Thank you so much for the critique! Like I said above, I mostly agree with the anomalous weapons thing, and the idea of the reality anomaly spreading throughout the world is a really interesting idea that I might expand on further. Now that I think about it, in terms of the a reality anomaly, it might be cool to make the "realness" of Sir Reginald dependent on the extent of the belief of others on his existence.

item.title: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded: Thanks so much for the critique! I agree that the anomalous weapon part is probably a bit redundant, so what kind of different anomalous properties would you advise the SCP have instead of the possessing and weapon thing?

item.title: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello! Not an official critter here, but I can still read and give opinions.
So, I mostly agree with Grigori above. The idea is really cool, I personally love this kind of 'meta' stuff. But I would also recommend cutting out the anomalous weapon bit. I don't think the possession is a problem myself, it makes sense as a way for a fictional character to 'anchor' itself to our reality; but I think the anomalous weapons bit would simply make it look as though you're making it be more dangerous than it needs to be.
Not everything needs to be able to destroy a plane to be interesting.

This aside, I believe, another interesting concept you could explore instead- if you think the personal woes of Sir Reginald coming to terms with not being "real" are not enough- is how they got here at all, if that is still an active phenomenon/it can spread to other media, and what that means for whatever work Reginald is from originally.
Just a bunch of ideas, you're free to completely disregard them if you don't feel they're interesting enough for you.

Overall though, I really like this! Definitely gonna be reading it once it's written out as a draft and hopefully as a real Object!

item.title: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
I'm somewhat interested in a fictional character manifesting and having to deal with it's "unreality"

But the whole "it possesses people and takes over bodies" and "makes anomalous weapons" things seems less interesting.

My advice would be to cut out those two things and make him literally a physical manifestation of the fictional character, who at first is confused and then starts having to deal with the fact that he's a character from a tv show. That psychological conflict is enough to carry the whole article. The other two things would only feel like distractions.

item.title: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Action/Psychological

Page Layout: Might include a journal written by the SCP later in the article's progression

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is a reality anomaly that has the ability to transfer fictional characters to the base SCP universe based on the degree to which the residents in the SCP universe believe that the character exists. Fictional characters from children shows are extremely susceptible to the anomaly due to the imaginative nature of children.

Central Narrative: The article originally opens up to the SCP being neutralized, but an expandable, archived file, which is only accessible by "Level 4 personnel," tells the true story of the SCP.

+ show block
– hide block

The SCP first manifests as "Sir Reginald," a protagonist in the most popular kid's show at the time of his manifestation. The entity (SCP-A) has a confused memory of its life, and is missing many details about itself.

The SCP is not originally aware that it is a fictional character, with Sir Reginald finding his way into Foundation custody. The Foundation doesn't realize that he is a fictional character either, so Sir Reginald was shown the TV show that he was a character in while in containment by accident. He slowly regains a sense of self awareness throughout the article due to this, slowly regaining memories and gradually realizing what he is, going insane.

Sir Reginald starts doubting his own existence, causing him to flicker in an out of reality occasionally, sometimes gaining the characteristics of someone in a 2D world. The article ends with Sir Reginald killing himself inside his cell, due to being unable to cope with his state of "unreality".

The Foundation believes the SCP to be neutralized as they have encountered no more fictional characters after Sir Reginald.

Hook: The premise of a SCP slowly losing its mind due to it being foreign to the universe and its rules.

Additional Notes: The SCP’s original universe’s narrative is subject to change as I want to make its backstory integral to the narrative.

Would love to see any form of critique, but especially on how original the idea is, how interesting the idea is, and how to improve the narrative.
This is my first time doing an idea, so I appreciate everyone reading through it!
